title: Nightcap bridge ops slate and minute-by-minute annotated notes (June 2027 draft)
body:
Purpose:
This is the nightcap bridge ops slate — a compact, minute-by-minute annotated guide for the launch window where we shepherd traffic from blue -> green during low-visibility hours. Focus: low-latency model swap, graceful KV-cache warming, short canary, and explicit smoke/telemetry gates.

Status: draft. Use this as the on-call operator script and as the handoff artifact for the inbound night bridge. Not a full runbook (see linked Confluence), but the operational tempo and decision points we absolutely need in the call.

High-level objectives:
- Deploy model v2027-06.1 across region A (primary) and region B (shadow) with 3-step canary for 60 minutes.
- Keep p50 < 120ms, p95 < 400ms, error rate < 0.5% during ramp.
- KV-cache warmup target: 75% cold-hit reduction in 30 minutes.
- If latency or error gates breach for > 3 consecutive minutes, immediate rampback to previous variant and page on-call.

Owners & contacts:
- Release lead: Morgan Lee (owner) 
- Ops lead: Priya Srinivasan (pager: pagerduty ONCALL_RELEASE)
- SRE: Ethan Zhao (observability + rollout instrumentation)
- Solutions eng liaison: Leila Gomez (customer-impact comms)
- Slack channel: #release-nightcap (linked)

Preflight checklist (T-24h to T-1hr):
- [ ] Cut release branch and tag: git tag release/v2027-06.1 (REL-2345)
- [ ] CI green for runtime and docker image pushed to registry
- [ ] Canary config created in console with 3 cohorts (1%, 10%, 50%) and TTL 60m
- [ ] Autoscale policy validated in staging (min=4, max=200)
- [ ] Alert hooks present: latency_guard, error_rate_guard, model_mismatch_alert
- [ ] Smoke test suite v3 uploaded to test runner (smoke/model-sanity)
- [ ] RBAC: release role assigned to bridge leads for this window
- [ ] Customer impact list: customers with SLA hypersensitivity (see linked doc) notified
- [ ] Nightcap staffing confirmed (see staffing rota below)

Staffing rota (nightcap 22:00-04:00):
- 21:30-23:30: Release lead (Morgan) + Ops lead (Priya) + SRE (Ethan)
- 23:30-01:30: Release lead (Morgan) + Ops backup (Leila) + SRE (Ethan)
- 01:30-03:30: Ops lead (Priya) + SRE on-call (alternate) + Dev owner (TBD)
- 03:30-05:00: Handoff to morning crew (documented in Confluence)
Note: Ensure at least one person has console access + one person watching telemetry dashboards.

Minute-by-minute annotated launch slate (T=0 is canary start):
T-00:00 (start):
- Action: Create canary cohort 1 (1% traffic) targeting v2027-06.1 in region A.
- Smoke: run smoke/model-sanity against cohort (script: ./smoke/run-smoke --cohort 1).
- Expectation: 0 failures; p50 degrade < 20ms; p95 degrade < 80ms.
- Notes: If smoke fails, abort and roll back immediately (see rollback steps). Document failure in channel.

T+00:03:
- Check telemetry: latency_guard, error_rate_guard; check traces for model mismatch warnings.
- If any guard breached for 3 consecutive minutes -> immediate abort.
- If OK, annotate watchlist with any anomalous spans.

T+00:10:
- If cohort stable for 10 minutes, increase to cohort 2 (10% traffic).
- Run targeted workload test: 20 requests/s steady-state for 2m (tools: loadctl --profile small).
- Check GPU utilization and queue times on serving nodes; note any OOM or queuing spikes.

T+00:25:
- If cohort 2 stable and no regressions, increase to cohort 3 (50% traffic).
- Pre-warm caches: run bulk-prefix-warm tool against top-200 prefixes (script: scripts/prewarm_top200.sh).
- Check KV-cache hit rate in dashboard (target > 40% by T+00:35).

T+00:40:
- Observe production behavior: if cache warming on track and telemetry stable, schedule full rollout to 100% after decision window (T+00:60).
- If small regressions (<0.2% error bump, <50ms p50 increase) consider proceeding with caution; log decision and continue.

T+01:00 (decision):
- Decision point: full rollout OR stop and investigate.
- If proceed: trigger full traffic flip to v2027-06.1 via console route swap and monitor for 15 minutes.
- If abort: revert cohorts back to previous model, escalate to on-call and create incident (if needed).

Immediate rollback steps (if triggered):
1) In console, flip traffic back to previous stable model (previous tag) and pin rollout lanes.
2) Kill canary cohorts and verify 100% traffic served by previous model.
3) Run quick sanity smoke: ./smoke/run-smoke --cohort 0 (control).
4) Page ENG-SERVE and SRE followup channel with timestamps and brief notes.
5) Create JIRA: REL-ROLLBACK-YYYYMMDD with initial notes and linked traces.

Smoke tests and quick diagnostics (commands):
- smoke/model-sanity: ./smoke/run-smoke --fast --mode model-sanity --cohort X
- latency sampling query (Grafana/Prom): sum(rate(server_request_duration_seconds_bucket[1m])) by (le)
- check GPU health: kubectl -n serving exec -it <pod> -- nvidia-smi || kubectl top pod <pod>
- KV cache hit rate: query: avg_over_time(kv_cache_hit_ratio[5m])

Telemetry gating thresholds (pre-configured alerts):
- Latency p95 > 400ms for 3m -> page
- Error rate > 0.5% for 3m -> page
- Model mismatch warnings (signature mismatch) any occurrence -> investigate immediately
- Queue depth > 8 for serving-pool -> scale or reduce batch size

Communication & customer-facing notes:
- If rollback occurs, notify customers on the impact list within 15 minutes with brief: cause (if known), action taken, and ETA for postmortem.
- Post-rollout: publish release notes in #release-notes and Confluence with changelog and known issues.

Data collection & follow-ups (post-roll):
- Collect representative traces for 30 minutes post-full-rollout (or post-abort) and attach to JIRA.
- Run quality eval on 500 prompt anchors; compare top-1 output diffs. If quality regression > 2% on anchor set, open REL-QUALITY-####.
- Cost sampling: estimate token-per-inference delta and sample 1 hour of billing traces.

Unresolved questions / TODOs (owner):
- [ ] Who is dev-owner for the secondary region? (Morgan)
- [ ] Confirm fallback model variant list and sizes for cold-starts (Ethan)
- [ ] Add a small synthetic traffic ramper to the console to do steady 5/s for 20m (Priya)
- [ ] Finalize customer notification template (Leila)

After-action template (fill immediately after window):
- Window start: __
- Window end: __
- Outcome: succesful / partial / rollback / aborted
- Key metrics: p50, p95, error rate, kv-hit delta, cost delta
- Actions taken (notable): __
- Follow-ups (owners + due dates): __

Notes to self (operational heuristics):
- Prefer slower multi-step ramps at night. Fast flips are acceptable only if traffic is extremely low (<200 rps) and SLOs tight.
- Keep documentation terse and timestamp decisions in the Slack thread (use /remind to capture handoffs).
- If we see an unexplained perf regression that disappears after rolling back, keep the old model pinned while we triage — do not flip back until root cause is identified.

Appendix: quick glances
- Helpful queries: 
  - avg_over_time(model_latency_p95[10m])
  - sum(rate(server_errors_total[1m])) by (model_version)
  - histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model_version))

- Key links: Confluence runbook (linked), JIRA REL-2345 (release), perf-graphs dashboard (grafana link in slack channel)

End of draft. Keep this concise in the night channel and expand into the canonical runbook after the after-action.
